purpose: Named product-level examples in which a regulator-authored or regulator-hosted source documents material use of a NAM in regulatory decision-making. This dataset is broader than animal-study displacement: every record explicitly states what evidence was displaced or supplemented, and records that did not replace animal studies must not be counted as animal displacement.

cases.indication: HLA-A*02:01-positive unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma
cases.nam: Human tissue and cell-based in vitro assays assessing target/species specificity, cross-reactivity in 35 human tissues, organ-specific toxicity potential in 13 tissues, cytokines and cytolytic proteins
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported the safety of clinical trials in the absence of a pharmacologically relevant animal model and contributed to development leading to approval.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Pharmacologically relevant animal model was unavailable; the human in vitro assay suite supplied nonclinical safety and mechanistic evidence needed to support clinical development.
cases.cross_jurisdiction_note: EMA states that tebentafusp is human-specific and that there are no relevant animal species for nonclinical toxicology. TGA states that omission of animal-species toxicity studies was justified by human specificity and absence of equivalent targets, while describing the supporting human target-binding, tissue-panel and cytokine evidence. Health Canada's independent Summary Basis of Decision likewise states that tebentafusp is human-specific, that no relevant animal species existed for nonclinical toxicology, and that long-term carcinogenicity, genotoxicity and reproductive/developmental toxicity studies were not conducted. This makes Kimmtrak a four-regulator cross-jurisdiction precedent rather than an FDA-only anecdote.
cases.note: FDA/CDER/OND authors explicitly identify Kimmtrak as a NAM regulatory-decision example and state that the human tissue/cell assay suite supported clinical-trial safety in the absence of pharmacologically relevant animal models. EMA, TGA and Health Canada independently corroborate the absence of a relevant animal species and the corresponding nonclinical strategy. This remains different from a one-for-one waiver of a named mandatory animal study.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Human-based methods have already supported named drug programs when relevant animal models were unavailable
The same scientific constraint and alternative evidence strategy can be recognized independently across regulators

cases.nam: In vitro characterization and safety studies, literature-based on-target/off-tumour assessment, human-membrane-protein/off-target assays, and clinical evidence for a patient-specific BCMA-directed CAR-T product
cases.regulatory_impact: EMA accepted a nonclinical safety package without formal GLP toxicology and without repeat-dose toxicity studies because no relevant animal model was available; PMDA independently concluded that Carvykti has no pharmacologically relevant rodent or nonhuman-primate species because of absent BCMA cross-reactivity and evaluated a tailored package including human-membrane and other in vitro safety assays.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: EMA: formal GLP toxicology and repeat-dose toxicity studies were not performed; a cynomolgus model was explicitly considered non-relevant. PMDA: no pharmacologically relevant rodent or NHP species existed for Carvykti itself, although a mouse xenograft model was used for selected pharmacology/off-target observations.
cases.cross_jurisdiction_note: EMA provides the clearest displacement statement: no GLP formal toxicology, no repeat-dose toxicology, and explicit acceptance of the absence because no relevant model existed. PMDA independently states that Carvykti lacks cross-reactivity to rodent and NHP BCMA and therefore has no pharmacologically relevant animal species, while reviewing tailored in vitro human-membrane/off-target assays and a limited mouse xenograft model. PMDA corroborates species irrelevance and tailored NAM reliance but should not be described as an identical animal-free toxicology decision.
cases.note: This is omission of conventional formal toxicology rather than a completely animal-free development program. Some in vivo proof-of-concept and non-GLP animal work existed. Health Canada's later authorization documents human-cell in vitro functional assays and in vitro approaches to insertional-mutagenesis risk but does not make the same explicit repeat-dose-omission statement.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Named advanced-therapy approvals can proceed without conventional formal animal toxicology when the models are scientifically non-relevant and alternative evidence addresses risk

cases.indication: CD19-positive B-cell malignancies within the authorised indications
cases.nam: Product-specific in vitro expansion/transformation studies, genomic insertion-site analysis and tailored evidence for a patient-specific genetically modified T-cell product, integrated with nonstandard in vivo pharmacology where informative
cases.regulatory_impact: CHMP accepted the absence of standard single-dose and repeat-dose toxicity studies because tisagenlecleucel is patient-specific and not appropriate to administer to immunocompetent animals; it also considered conventional rodent genotoxicity/carcinogenicity models inappropriate and noted that animal germline-transmission studies of genetically modified human cells are not recommended.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Standard single-dose toxicity, repeat-dose toxicity and conventional rodent genotoxicity/carcinogenicity testing were not used as the relevant safety strategy; comparative in vivo pharmacology for a manufacturing-site comparability change was also considered inappropriate and unnecessary.
cases.note: CHMP's public assessment report directly states that lack of single-dose toxicity studies was acceptable because the patient-specific product is not appropriate for immunocompetent animals and that repeat-dose studies were likewise acceptable to omit for a single-infusion patient-specific product. In vitro and genomic analyses were used for transformation/insertional-risk questions, while immunocompromised-mouse studies were used for selected persistence/tumour-growth questions. This is not an animal-free development program.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Omission of conventional toxicology is not isolated to one CAR-T product but appears across approved patient-specific advanced therapies when model relevance is poor

cases.nam: Cell-based complement assays and validated ex vivo CH50 hemolysis assay
cases.regulatory_impact: Mechanistic nonclinical NAM data, together with correlating clinical data, served as confirmatory evidence supporting substantial evidence of efficacy and approval.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: FDA authors state that no pharmacologically relevant species existed for key complement pharmacology; cell-based and ex vivo assays were therefore central to demonstrating pharmacodynamic activity.
cases.note: Do not count as pure animal-study displacement: FDA's totality-of-evidence description also includes animal and human data. The significance is regulator-confirmed NAM reliance within a named approval where a pharmacologically relevant species was absent for the key mechanism.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Regulatory adoption can take the form of NAM evidence filling questions that relevant species cannot answer

cases.indication: Cystic fibrosis subpopulations defined by responsive CFTR variants
cases.nam: In vitro CFTR chloride-transport assays using mutant CFTR systems including human bronchial epithelial cells
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported expansion to specific CFTR variants without additional clinical trials for each variant; FDA accepted a defined in vitro response threshold linked to prior clinical efficacy.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: Important NAM adoption precedent but not animal displacement. Preserve this distinction in all counts and figures.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Validated NAM evidence can become reusable enough to extend regulatory decisions to otherwise impractical subpopulations

cases.indication: Fabry disease with amenable GLA variants
cases.nam: In vitro alpha-galactosidase A activity assay in cells expressing specific GLA variants
cases.regulatory_impact: FDA accepted assay-response thresholds to identify amenable variants and expand the indicated genetic population without separate pre-approval clinical trials for every variant, with a post-approval clinical verification requirement.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: Important NAM adoption precedent but not animal displacement. FDA required post-approval clinical verification, illustrating that regulatory reliance can be conditional and staged.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Regulatory reliance can be staged: a validated in vitro model can support approval while residual uncertainty is handled through post-approval evidence generation
